Senses.Explanation: Toward or facing (向), above or further up (上), and matter or affair (事): the upward matter. It runs in a recurrent dialogue. A monk asks whether there is still an upward matter (向上還有事也無／還有向上事也無); the master says yes; the monk asks, 'What is the upward matter?' (如何是向上事); and the master gives an answer such as 'break the mirror and come; I will meet you' (打破鏡來，與汝相見), 'a person from Silla does not wrap his head' (新羅人不褁頭), or 'downward the text runs long' (向下文長). It also appears in 'knows that there is an upward matter' (知有向上事, 69 occurrences) and its negation. One line says that Xuefeng had words only after he knew there was an upward matter (雪峯知有向上事始有語話分). The expression can be dismissed with 'What upward matter are you talking about?' (說甚麼向上事). The corpus also attaches 'upward' to named limits: 'the matter upward from buddha' (佛向上事, 149 occurrences) and 'upward from Vairocana' (毘盧向上). It is paired with 'the last word' (末後句) in the statement that one must also know the upward matter and the last word (更須知有向上事末後句始得). Related forms include 'the upward road' (向上一路, 957), 'the upward move' (向上一著, 279), 'the upward aperture' (向上一竅, 270), 'the upward pivot' (向上關捩子, 101), 'the upward person' (向上人, 229), and 'the upward vehicle of the lineage' (向上宗乘, 462).
Senses.Note: A corpus-wide term, with 1,363 hits in 222 allowlist texts. The full dialogue—whether there is an upward matter, yes, then what it is—recurs across houses. The word 'upward' (向上) is relative to whatever the text has just named, as shown by 'the matter beyond Buddha' (佛向上事) and 'beyond Vairocana' (毘盧向上).

Occurrences.Kwic: 曰。如何是向上事。師曰。打破鏡來。與汝相見。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Five Lamps Meeting the Source (五燈會元), Lingyun Zhiqin section. Changsheng Jiaoran remains the named exact questioner through the complete exchange and asks what the upward matter is; Lingyun answers, 'break the mirror and come; I will meet you.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 此人還知有向上事也無。師曰。不知。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), Zhaozhou Congshen section. An unnamed questioner asks whether this person knows there is an upward matter; Zhaozhou answers, 'does not know.' The six-rung ladder does not name the questioner.

Occurrences.Kwic: 更須知有向上事末後句始得
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 古尊宿語錄, Foyan Qingyuan's recorded sayings. Foyan Qingyuan is the exact speaker: in his hall address he says that even after seeing colors clearly one must know the matter beyond and the final phrase before study is finished.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧云向上還有事也無師云有僧云如何是向上事師云新羅人不褁頭
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), in Shoushan Xingnian's section. An unnamed monk is the exact speaker who asks whether there is an upward matter and then asks what the upward matter is; Shoushan answers first 'yes' and then 'a person from Silla does not wrap his head.' The line, expanded context, section header, book title, TEI header, exact full-case search, and parallel passages do not name this monk.
